newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus no comment on stalled status change report.
newsitem.headline: Airbus no comment on stalled status change report.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus said late on Sunday it could not confirm or deny a German newspaper report that plans to change the aircraft partnership into an integrated commercial company had been put on hold.
"I have no information to confirm or deny this report," an Airbus spokesman said.

Germany's Welt am Sonntag reported on Sunday that Airbus Industrie's supervisory board had decided at a May 27 meeting in Toulouse, France, to freeze the strategic change in status that had been announced in January.
The newspaper, noting the meeting's results had not yet been made public, said talks had become bogged down over how to split up the mix of civil and military programmes.
An industry source said the German report appeared to be an exercise in testing the response of the Airbus partners. "It looks like the Germans are flying a kite," he said.
Relations between the Airbus partners have been strained while the restructuring talks have been going on.
Airbus is a partnership between French state-owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
